title: Review of New Zealand's smokefree generation law for Singapore
asked: Ms He Ting Ru asked whether the Ministry has reviewed the impact of New Zealand's smokefree generation law and whether it would be appropriate and effective in Singapore.
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said New Zealand has withdrawn its plans for a smoke-free generation law, and Singapore will continue to monitor international developments and learn from other countries' tobacco control experience. She set out Singapore's existing multi-prong strategy, including policy measures, public preventive education, cessation programmes and tax prohibitions, and said smoking prevalence reached an all-time low of 8.4% in 2024. She noted that Malaysia removed its announced plan and that the UK announced plans in October 2023 for a generation unable to legally purchase tobacco in their lifetime. She said Singapore remains open to the policy, will announce any movements, is engaging Dr Koong Heng Nung, and will study developments in other countries.

key_points.point: New Zealand has withdrawn its plans for a smoke-free generation law.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: New Zealand has withdrawn their plans for a smoke-free generation law.

key_points.point: Singapore will continue to monitor international developments and learn from other countries' tobacco control experience.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We will continue to monitor international developments and learn from the experiences of other countries in the area of tobacco control.

key_points.point: Singapore's existing strategy includes policy measures, public preventive education, cessation programmes and tax prohibitions.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: This includes having a comprehensive mix of policy measures, public preventive education, as well as cessation programmes, including also our tax prohibitions.

key_points.point: Smoking prevalence reached an all-time low of 8.4% in 2024.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we have achieved an all-time low of 8.4% in 2024.

key_points.point: Malaysia announced a similar plan and then removed it.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Malaysia, also, who had announced it, had also removed it.

key_points.point: The UK announced plans in October 2023 for a generation that will not be legally able to purchase tobacco in their lifetime.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: UK had announced plans in October 2023 for a generation that will not be legally able to purchase tobacco in their lifetime.

key_points.point: Singapore remains open to the policy and will announce any movements.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We are continuing to be open to this. We will announce if there are any movements in this front.

key_points.point: The ministry continues engagement with Dr Koong Heng Nung, the original advocate of tobacco-free generation.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we continue to be in engagement with Dr Koong Heng Nung, who was the original advocate of tobacco-free generation

key_points.point: Singapore will study developments in other countries.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We will study and see what the developments are in the other countries.

key_points.point: There are concerns about how the policy would be implemented.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We have concerns about how the implementation will be carried out
